FoBA 2026 is the premier event for Business Analysts who want to focus on outcomes that move organisations forward.

Adapt. Align. Accelerate.

In a world defined by constant change, AI, automation, and rapidly evolving technology, traditional ways of working are no longer enough. FoBA 2026 challenges professionals to adapt how they think and work, strengthening strategic thinking and applying business analysis tools and techniques in ways the world now requires. Adapt by evolving your skills, mindset, and approach. Use insight, data, and analysis to understand complex problems before rushing to solutions.
Align by connecting strategy, people, and delivery. Facilitate the right conversations, influence priorities, and ensure effort is focused on what creates the most value.
Accelerate by increasing momentum through strategic decision making, purposeful use of techniques, and modern ways of working. Focus not on doing more, but on doing what matters.

long_description:
Overview

A multisport event for kids aged between 4 - 18 years from all around the region.

The kids duathlon is back again for 2026!

We are delighted to have the support of Brancott Estate Vineyard who offer us their beautiful, off-road vineyard setting for the Harcourts Marlborough Kids Duathlon.

Brancott Estate Vineyard, 180 Brancott Road, Fairhall, Blenheim

The Duathlon will operate regardless of weather conditions. The entry fee per child is payable upon registration. You must select what course you want your child to take part in. There are 3 options available this year.

Short Race Run 1km | Bike 3km | Run 1km

Course is open to kids 6-18yrs. You are welcome to walk or run. Choose your course according to your age and fitness level. Please note that distances are approximate.

Long Race Run 2km | Bike 5.5km | Run 1km

Course is open to kids 6-18yrs. You are welcome to walk or run. Choose your course according to your age and fitness level. Please note that distances are approximate.

Beat the Bear 500m walk/run

Course is open to kids 4-7yrs. Parents are welcome to join their child on this one if they wish to support and encourage.

Race Number Collection

We recommend you collect your race number and t-shirt (if you ordered one) before the day, as it will be very busy at the venue.

Race numbers and t-shirts will be available at Bike Fit Marlborough, 24 Market Street, Blenheim on Saturday 17th of October from 10am and 12pm and at the venue on Sunday 18th October between 8:30am – 9am.

Start times

Beat the Bear 9.20am

Short Race 9.40am

Long Race 10.15am

All races will start when previous particpants have finished the course, so times may vary.

We ask that everyone please be present for the briefing which starts at 9:15am at the finish area. All bikes must be ready and in transition by 9.00 am

Drinks and water

To minimise waste and our environmental impact, please bring your own reusable drink bottle. There will be water available to refill your bottle on site.

T Shirts

The 2026 collectors t-shirt is available in sizes 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, adult medium, large and extra large. T-shirts must be pre-ordered and paid at time of entry. T-shirt orders are not available after 30th September 2026.

Entries close

14th October 2026. Limited registrations will be taken on the day. Any entries after 14 October are not eligible for spot prize draws. Entries are strictly limited to 500 and will be accepted on a first-come-first-served basis.

Race briefing and rules

Briefing starts at 9:15am at the Finish area. All participants are eligible for the major spot prizes of a bike and helmet from bike fit. Every race number will go into the draw that we do on the day but participants must be present at prize giving to claim them.

A list of other spot prize winners will be displayed and prizes available for collection at the registration tent. Late entries (after 14th October) are not eligible for minor spot prizes, sorry.

Refunds

We are not able to refund any entry fees after the closing date or t-shirt payments after 30th September 2026.

long_description:
Overview

Learn ways to resolve conflict with customers and co-workers, influence successful outcomes and develop a peaceful workplace.

Transform conflict and difficult situations, people/customers into opportunities by equipping your staff with the skills and techniques required to manage these situations with confidence, professionalism and pride.

We have all experienced the stress that comes from having unresolved conflicts with our customers and co-workers. Conflicts that are ignored or resolved poorly don’t go away, they cause people to feel resentful and to avoid each other. The effects on the business are a loss of productivity, turnover and absenteeism. Wherever two or more people come together, there is bound to be conflict. This workshop will give participants a six-step process that they can use and modify to resolve conflicts of any size. Participants will also learn crucial conflict resolution skills, including dealing with anger and using the Agreement Frame.


Learning Outcomes:

Transform conflict into opportunity
Develop constructive strategies for dealing with difficult behavior
Develop communication skills to diffuse the situation
Increase confidence and assertiveness in dealing with difficult behaviour
Manage your emotions and deal with stress
Understand the power of words and how to use them to your advantage


For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 04 974 8790

long_description:
Overview

An opportunity to join a workshop led by artist Wayne Youle specifically aimed at educators.

“The toughest part as an artist (for me at least) is the unlocking of ideas...the starting of something, the loosening of both body and mind.”

Artist Wayne Youle has decades of experience creating across a number of disciplines, and is always deeply engaged with his community through teaching workshops across multiple age groups. While his exhibition Back in Five is showing at The Dowse, teachers have the opportunity to join a workshop led by Youle specifically aimed at educators. Consisting of multiple shorter activities, the workshop will focus on ways to engage students’ creative sparks, working together on a project rather than focusing on individual ownership, emphasising the process rather than the finished piece, and breaking down any preciousness when it comes to sharing.

long_description:
Overview

The health and safety reforms are coming. If your business hasn't got its head around what that means yet, now is the time.

Critical Conversations with Site Safe CE, Brett Murray

The health and safety reforms are coming, and critical risk management is set to be WorkSafe's number one focus going forward. If your business hasn't got its head around what that means yet, now's the time.




That's why Site Safe Chief Executive Brett Murray is taking to the road this September and October to talk directly with the industry about what's ahead - and how to prepare for it.




This is a free, in-person event for construction and safety professionals across the regions, built around three things we think matter:

· A fireside chat with Brett Murray on the H&S reforms:

As the former head of WorkSafe’s High Hazard Unit, Brett brings an extensive background in health and safety regulation, and he'll walk through what the reforms mean in practice. Brett will focus on the shift towards understanding and managing critical risks, and what that obligation will look like for your business. This will be followed by an open Q&A, so bring your questions.

· A chance to meet your local Site Safe team

Stick around afterwards and take the opportunity to meet your regional manager and your local Site Safe Safety Advisor. These are valuable contacts to have on hand for local health and safety support.

· Food, drinks, and networking

The event is fully catered, with time built in to connect with other safety-minded construction companies in your region.




Spaces are limited, so please register to secure your seat.




Other events:

During this roadshow, Brett will also take Critical Conversations to the following regions. Pass this invitation along to your nationally based colleagues or peers.

Dunedin - Tuesday 15 September

Invercargill - Tuesday 15 September

Queenstown - Wednesday 16 September

Nelson - Wednesday 7 October

Taranaki - Friday 16 October

Palmerston North - Monday 19 October

Hawke's Bay - Tuesday 20 October

long_description:
Overview

Decode your mind through the Enneagram and discover new ways to understand yourself, navigate differences and deepen your relationships.

Inspire me workshops




The Blueprint of the Mind- understanding yourself through the Enneagram




You may know the situation when your partner, friend, boss or spouse does things or says things where you might wonder how this person could ever say/do things like that, because it's completely opposite of how you would handle the exact same situation.

The result of it is often endless frustration, disappointment, misunderstandings and many more emotional disturbances due to seeing the world fundamentally different from other persons that we're dealing with.

If we, however get a better understanding of the core mentality, fears and desires of different types of people that are in our environment incl our own triggers and blinds pots, dealing with people will be so much easier and it will lay the foundation for much more meaningful and deep relationships.

In this workshop we'll discover different aspects of the Enneagram, which is an ancient map of nine personality types - nine different core motivations and fears that quietly shape how we think, feel and react in our day to day life.
If you want to understand your own strengths and points of improvements while also being able to relate to the people in your environment better, come to our workshop

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host Gopi

Gopi helps spiritually minded professionals achieve clarity, overcome negative thought patterns and habits through his unique integration of hypnotherapy and palmistry. During his former life as a monk, he delved into the timeless wisdom of astrology, palmistry, and the ancient knowledge of the mind and consciousness, gaining deep insights into human psychology. He combines these powerful teachings with modern, effective tools as a certified practitioner in applied hypnotherapy, trauma informed coach, along with the knowledge he gained through his diploma in psychology and counseling.

long_description:
Overview

Quiet the mind, open the heart, and reconnect with our highest self through Kundalini Yoga, breathwork, meditation and sound.

This workshop is part of an 8-part chakra journey across 2026. Each session stands alone or can be experienced as part of the full series.

Join us for an uplifting afternoon as we explore the Crown Chakra (Sahasrara) through the transformative practices of Kundalini Yoga and the deeply restorative sounds of a Gong Bath.

The Crown Chakra is the centre of connection, awareness, peace, and spiritual consciousness. When balanced, it helps us experience a sense of purpose, inner peace, and connection to something greater than ourselves. Through movement, breathwork, meditation, and sound, we'll create space to quiet the mind, open the heart, and reconnect with our highest self.

🧘‍♀️Kundalini Yoga | 1:30pm – 3:00pm

Experience a 90-minute Kundalini Yoga class designed to activate and balance the Crown Chakra through breathwork (Pranayama), dynamic movement and postures, meditation, and deep relaxation.

☕Herbal Tea Break | 3:00pm – 3:30pm

Take time to relax, enjoy a cup of herbal tea, oracle cards and connect with others in a welcoming and supportive environment.

🎶Gong Bath | 3:30pm – 4:30pm

Lie back, get comfortable, and allow the soothing sounds and vibrations of the gong to guide you into a deeply restorative state of relaxation. A gong bath can help calm the nervous system, release stress, and leave you feeling refreshed and centred.

✨Choose the experience that suits you—you are welcome to attend either the yoga or the gong bath sessions or enjoy the full afternoon.

💫Suitable for beginners and experienced practitioners alike - no experience with yoga or sound healing needed. Modifications are offered throughout the yoga class.

💫 Bring an open heart, a yoga mat, blanket, water bottle and anything you need to feel cozy + supported.

✨Whether you're joining the entire afternoon or just one session, you'll leave feeling calmer, clearer, and more deeply connected to yourself.

This workshop offers a beautiful opportunity to pause, recharge, and reconnect.

Spaces are limited, so bookings are recommended.

Investment:

$35 Yoga | $30 Gong Bath | $55 Both

Special discounted ticket option: $100 two person special - bring a friend with you to attend the yoga and the gong session. Must select this ticket option for the discount to apply (i.e. both people must book together)

If you want to pay by cash on the day or by bank transfer, please send an email to mel@prosperityyoga.co.nz to book your place.

long_description:
Overview

'It's in the Ballot' takes the format of the Kiwi TV classic 'It's in the Bag' game show and puts a political twist to it.

Contestants of 'It's in the Bag' become political candidates in 'It's in the Ballot' Meet the Candidates.

Candidates choose a numbered box which has a question that has been submitted online by voters before the show.

It’s in the Ballot” is a community-led awareness and participation initiative. We aim to increase voter interest in the general and council elections nationally.

By using broadcasting and web-based technologies to deliver in-studio; online on Facebook, YouTube and Twitch; and edited as YouTube videos we aim to enable voters to make informed voting decisions.

This means you can send the weblink of the YouTube Video of your electorate show to your friends and whanau to encourage them to watch the show before they cast their votes.

Enrolments cut off date is Sunday 25th October 2026

Enrol at - https://vote.nz/enrolling/enrol-or-update/enrol-or-update-online

Early voting starts Monday 26th October 2026

Election Day is Saturday 7th November 2026
